latest_release.name: FRadioPlayer 0.4.0
latest_release.body:
FRadioPlayer 0.4.0 brings Swift 6 and main-actor isolation to the library, with fixes for seeking, interruptions, stale artwork, and audio-session setup.

## Highlights

- **Swift 6, main-actor player**: player state and observer callbacks are main-actor isolated. AVFoundation callbacks that arrive off-main cross to the main actor before changing state.
- **Playback intent is preserved**: seeking and interruptions no longer override a user's pause or stop.
- **Audio-session ownership is configurable**: apps that manage their own session can set `FRadioPlayer.configuresAudioSession = false` on the main actor, before the first access to `shared`. The default remains `true`.

## Breaking changes

- **Xcode 16+ / Swift 6 toolchain required.** The library builds in Swift 6 language mode; your app can stay in Swift 5 mode.
- **Call the player from the main actor**, including in Swift 5 apps. Add `@MainActor` to your controller, or hop with `Task { @MainActor in ... }` from a nonisolated context.
- **Seeking while paused or stopped no longer starts playback.** Call `play()` explicitly if your UI intends to resume after seeking.

## Fixed

- Seek completions run exactly once, asynchronously on the main actor, including without a loaded item, before duration is known, and when a seek is superseded. Seek positions retain subsecond precision.
- Interruptions resume only playback that was active when the interruption began, when the system allows it, and when the user has not since paused or stopped.
- Playback after a failed stream recovers on iOS 27 by omitting a redundant explicit asset timing option. Existing custom-header asset setup is preserved.
- Late artwork from a previous station or track is discarded.
- Failed loads report `.error` without a transient `.loadingFinished` notification.
- Audio-session setup uses valid `.playback` category options, fixing the category error observed on a physical iPhone.
- End-of-item, seek, and off-main KVO callbacks no longer mutate player state off the main actor. Late KVO from replaced items is ignored.

## Testing

- 56 macOS tests and 60 iOS tests cover API contracts, callback delivery, seeking, interruption intent, audio-session configuration, artwork, playback fixtures, and recovery.
- Full local suites passed on macOS, iOS 26.5, and iOS 27. The Swift 5 demo and tvOS library SDK builds passed.
- CI passed macOS tests, iOS simulator tests, the Swift 5 demo build, and the minimum Xcode 16 build. Simulator tests now wait for boot completion.
- Simulator notification tests cover state handling; headset, AirPlay, Bluetooth, and CarPlay routing still require physical-device validation.

## Demo app

- Main-actor controller and explicit actor hops in remote-command handlers.
- New app icon and Choice Classic Rock replaces the unavailable Classic Rock stream.

## Requirements

iOS 14+, macOS 11+, tvOS 14+, Swift 6 toolchain / Xcode 16+. Platform minimums are unchanged.

If your dependency is pinned to 0.3.0 or restricted to the 0.3 minor series, update it to receive this release:

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/fethica/FRadioPlayer.git", from: "0.4.0")
```

See the [0.4.0 migration guide](https://github.com/fethica/FRadioPlayer/blob/0.4.0/.github/release-notes/0.4.0.md) for controller isolation, observer callbacks, artwork providers, seeking, and audio-session ownership.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/fethica/FRadioPlayer/compare/0.3.0...0.4.0

detail.readme:
FRadioPlayer

FRadioPlayer is a wrapper around AVPlayer to handle internet radio playback. ## Example SwiftUI demo source lives under `Example/FRadioPlayerDemo/`. Use XcodeGen to generate and open the demo project: ```sh brew install xcodegen # once cd Example xcodegen # generates FRadioPlayerDemo.xcodeproj open FRadioPlayerDemo.xcodeproj ``` ## Features - [x] Support internet radio URL playback - [x] Update and parse track metadata - [x] Update and show album artwork (via iTunes API) - [x] Automatic handling of interruptions - [x] Automatic handling of route changes - [x] Support bluetooth playback - [x] Network interruptions handling - [x] Automatic stall recovery with bounded retries (reload with backoff, clean error state when the stream is gone) - [x] Host-managed recovery, classified failures and item seams for apps that own playback (0.5.0) - [x] Support for Swift Package Manager SPM ## Requirements - iOS 14.0+ - macOS 11.0+ - tvOS 14.0+ - Xcode 16+ (Swift 6 toolchain; the package builds in Swift 6 language mode, your app can stay in Swift 5 mode) ## Installation ### Swift Package Manager FRadioPlayer is available through [SPM](https://github.com/apple/swift-package-manager). To add it in Xcode: File > Add Packages… and use the URL of this repository. Or add the dependency in `Package.swift`: ```swift .package(url: "https://github.com/fethica/FRadioPlayer.git", from: "0.4.0") ``` ## Quick Start Add the package, then use the shared player and observe changes. ```swift import FRadioPlayer // Adopting FRadioPlayerObserver here makes the class main-actor isolated final class RadioController: NSObject, FRadioPlayerObserver { let player = FRadioPlayer.shared override init() { super.init() player.addObserver(self) player.enableArtwork = true // Optional (default true) player.isAutoPlay = true // Optional (default true) player.radioURL = URL(string: "https://your.station/stream.mp3") // Or manually control playback: player.play() } func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, playerStateDidChange state: FRadioPlayer.State) { print("Player state: \(state)") } } // From a nonisolated context, hop to the main actor Task { @MainActor in FRadioPlayer.shared.togglePlaying() // Play/Pause FRadioPlayer.shared.stop() // Stop FRadioPlayer.shared.volume = 0.8 // Set volume (0.0...1.0) } ``` ### Manual Prefer SPM. If needed, drag `Sources/FRadioPlayer` into your Xcode project. ## Concurrency Since 0.4.0 `FRadioPlayer` is bound to the main actor and the package builds in Swift 6 language mode. - Call the player from the main actor. From a background context, hop first: `Task { @MainActor in FRadioPlayer.shared.play() }`. - Observer callbacks arrive on the main actor. A class that adopts `FRadioPlayerObserver` in its declaration is inferred `@MainActor`. A conformance added in an extension keeps the type's own isolation and still compiles. - A controller that calls the player from its own methods must be main-actor isolated. Add `@MainActor` to the class, as the demo's `RadioPlayer` does. This applies in Swift 5 mode too: calling an isolated method from a nonisolated one is an error, not a warning. - `FRadioPlayer.State` and `FRadioPlayer.PlaybackState` are `Sendable`. `FRadioPlayer.Metadata` is not, because it carries `AVTimedMetadataGroup` values; keep it on the main actor. - Custom `FRadioArtworkAPI` providers receive a `@Sendable` completion and may call it from any queue. Existing providers written with a plain completion keep compiling. - AVFoundation and audio session callbacks that can arrive off the main thread are received `nonisolated` inside the library and hopped explicitly. Nothing is marked `@unchecked Sendable` or `nonisolated(unsafe)`. See the [0.4.0 release notes and migration guide](.github/release-notes/0.4.0.md) when upgrading from 0.3.x. ## Audio session On iOS and tvOS the player sets the shared `AVAudioSession` category to `.playback`, with the default mode and no category options, when `FRadioPlayer.shared` is first accessed. The playback category supports AirPlay and Bluetooth A2DP without additional options on iOS. An app that owns its audio session opts out on the main actor before its first access to `shared`, for example in its `App` initializer or `application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:)`: ```swift FRadioPlayer.configuresAudioSession = false ``` Setting it after `shared` exists has no effect. The player never activates or deactivates the session. ## Host-managed recovery and seams Since 0.5.0 an app that wants to own retries, interruptions or the audio pipeline can take them over. Every seam is opt-in: with the defaults the player behaves exactly as in 0.4.0. | Seam | Default | What it lets the host do | | --- | --- | --- | | `recoveryPolicy` | `.automatic` | `.hostManaged` stops the built-in 2/4/8 s reload ladder. The player only reports stalls. | | `radioPlayerDidDetectStall(_:reason:)` | no-op | Hear about `.bufferEmpty`, `.networkReconnected` and `.playbackStalledNotification` while playback is wanted, under either policy. | | `radioPlayer(_:bufferingDidChange:)` | no-op | Track waiting-for-data periods (deduplicated). Starts on `timeControlStatus` waiting or buffer-empty with playback wanted; ends on `timeControlStatus` playing or paused, pause, stop and failure. `isPlaybackLikelyToKeepUp` is not a source (it only drives the legacy `state`). | | `radioPlayer(_:didObserveProgress:)` | no-op | A tick every 0.5 s while time advances, for files and live streams (from attachment, even if the duration stays indefinite), for watchdogs. AVPlayer also ticks on start, stop and time jumps: compare successive times. | | `lastFailure`, `radioPlayer(_:didFail:)` | no-op | A classified `Failure` (`.notFound`, `.forbidden`, `.unauthorized`, `.network`, `.timeout`, `.decode`, `.stalledExhausted`, `.unknown`, plus domain, code and HTTP status) delivered before the `.error` state. | | `stop(discardingItem:)` | `stop()` keeps the item | `true` drops the item, metadata and artwork, so the next `play()` reconnects with a fresh item. | | `playerItemConfigurator` | `nil` | Configure every new `AVPlayerItem` before it is attached, for example to install an `audioMix`. | | `itemGeneration` | starts at 0 | Increments on every new item, to tell a fresh item from a reattached one. | | `resumesAfterInterruption`, `radioPlayer(_:interruptionEnded:)` | `true`, no-op | `false` keeps the player paused when an interruption ends; the callback says whether resuming is warranted. | A host that owns its retry ladder: ```swift @MainActor final class PlaybackAuthority: FRadioPlayerObserver { let player = FRadioPlayer.shared init() { player.recoveryPolicy = .hostManaged player.resumesAfterInterruption = false player.playerItemConfigurator = { item in item.audioMix = makeLoudnessMix(for: item) // your tap } player.addObserver(self) } func radioPlayerDidDetectStall(_ player: FRadioPlayer, reason: FRadioPlayer.StallReason) { scheduleRetry() // your backoff, which ends in retry() } func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, didFail failure: FRadioPlayer.Failure) { switch failure.kind { case .notFound, .decode: break // terminal: tell the user default: scheduleRetry() } } func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, interruptionEnded shouldResume: Bool) { if shouldResume { player.play() } } func retry() { player.stop(discardingItem: true) // reconnect, don't resume player.play() } } ``` Notes: - Callbacks arrive on the main actor. Don't drive the player from inside `didFail`; it runs before `.error` is published, so schedule the retry instead. - The configurator runs on the main actor for every new item (URL change, `play()` after an error, `play()` after `stop(discardingItem: true)`), never for a reattached one. Don't retain the item. A stop, discard or URL change made inside the configurator wins: that item is dropped, not attached. The same holds for one made from the `.loading` callback of the rebuild that follows `stop(discardingItem: true)`. Metadata already queued for a discarded or replaced item is dropped. - Switching `recoveryPolicy` to `.hostManaged` cancels a reload the library already scheduled. ## Usage ### Basics 1. Import `FRadioPlayer` ```swift import FRadioPlayer ``` 2. Get the singleton `FRadioPlayer` instance ```swift let player = FRadioPlayer.shared ``` 3. Observe player events (optional) ```swift final class MyObserver: NSObject, FRadioPlayerObserver { override init() { super.init() FRadioPlayer.shared.addObserver(self) } func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, playerStateDidChange state: FRadioPlayer.State) { // handle state change } } ``` 4. Set the radio URL ```swift player.radioURL = URL(string: "http://example.com/station.mp3") ``` ### Properties - `isAutoPlay: Bool` Auto-play when `radioURL` is set (default `true`). - `enableArtwork: Bool` Fetch album artwork via iTunes API (default `true`). - `artworkAPI: FRadioArtworkAPI` Artwork provider, default `iTunesAPI(artworkSize: 300)`. - `rate: Float?` Current `AVPlayer` rate. - `isPlaying: Bool` Convenience read-only state. - `state: FRadioPlayer.State` Player state. - `playbackState: FRadioPlayer.PlaybackState` Playback state. - `volume: Float?` Player volume, 0.0…1.0. - `httpHeaderFields: [String:String]?` HTTP headers for the underlying `AVURLAsset`. - `metadataExtractor: FRadioMetadataExtractor` Strategy to parse timed metadata. - `currentMetadata: FRadioPlayer.Metadata?` Last parsed timed metadata. - `currentArtworkURL: URL?` Last resolved artwork URL. - `duration: TimeInterval` Total duration, 0 for live streams. - `currentTime: Double` Current playback time in seconds. - `FRadioPlayer.configuresAudioSession: Bool` (static) Whether the player sets the audio session category, default `true`. See [Audio session](#audio-session). ### Playback controls - Play ```swift player.play() ``` - Pause ```swift player.pause() ``` - Stop ```swift player.stop() ``` - Toggle playing state ```swift player.togglePlaying() ``` - Seek (files with a known duration) ```swift player.seek(to: 30) { // Called exactly once, on the main actor } ``` The completion is always called exactly once, on the main actor, after `seek` returns. That includes a live stream or an item whose duration isn't known yet (no seek happens), no loaded item, and a seek that is superseded by a newer one. Seeking keeps the playback intent: a playing player keeps playing, a paused or stopped player stays that way, and a pause issued while the seek is in flight wins. For live streams, `pause()` keeps the item attached and resumes from the buffered position. `stop()` detaches the item and clears metadata and artwork, but keeps the item: the next `play()` reattaches that same item, it does not build a new one. To reconnect with a fresh asset and item, call `stop(discardingItem: true)` before `play()`. ### Observer methods - Player state ```swift func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, playerStateDidChange state: FRadioPlayer.State) ``` - Playback state ```swift func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, playbackStateDidChange state: FRadioPlayer.PlaybackState) ``` - Item change ```swift func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, itemDidChange url: URL?) ``` - Timed metadata ```swift func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, metadataDidChange metadata: FRadioPlayer.Metadata?) ``` - Artwork URL ```swift func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, artworkDidChange artworkURL: URL?) ``` - Duration and time updates ```swift func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, durationDidChange duration: TimeInterval) func radioPlayer(_ player: FRadioPlayer, playTimeDidChange currentTime: TimeInterval, duration: TimeInterval) ``` ## Swift Radio App For more complete app features, check out [Swift Radio App](https://github.com/analogcode/Swift-Radio-Pro) based on **FRadioPlayer**

## Development This repository uses Swift Package Manager for building and testing: ```sh swift build swift test ``` The test suite covers the public API contract, metadata extraction, the artwork API (stubbed, no network), playback against bundled fixtures, and state machine regressions. CI runs it on macOS and on an iOS simulator for pull requests, pushes to `main` and tags. Bug fixes should come with a failing test first. ## Author [@fethica](https://fethica.com) ## License FRadioPlayer is available under the MIT license. See the LICENSE file for more info.
